To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) COP1 interacts with SPA1 to form a protein complex; (2) SPA1 inhibits COP1 E3 ubiquitin-ligase activity on HY5 in a light-dependent fashion.
(a) COP1 is part of a protein complex, and (b) COP1 and SPA1 interact to alter HY5 stability.
COP1 acts in concert with SPA1 to regulate the activity of HY5 in response to light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate plant growth in response to light.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the photomorphogenesis process in plants.
the molecular mechanism of phytochrome-mediated regulation of light responses in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPA1 acts as a negative regulator of PHYA signaling by modulating COP1-mediated ubiquitin-dependent degradation of HY5.
COP1 acts in concert with PHYA to promote the degradation of HY5.
the COP1-SPAI interaction defines a critical regulatory step in PHYA-mediated regulation of HY activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPA1 is a critical regulator of PHYA-mediated responses to far red light.
PHYA-mediated light signaling and COP1-mediated photomorphogenesis are integrated through the interaction between SPA1 and COP1.

SPA1, as a component of the phytochrome signaling network, is a critical regulator for COP1-mediated ubiquitin ligase function and that the COP1-SPAI interaction is a critical step in PHYA-mediated regulation of HY-5 activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the COP1-phytochrome interaction is critical for PHYA signaling and that the COP1 E3 ubiquitin-ligase activity is regulated by the COP1-SPAI interaction.
the interaction between SPA1 and COP1 defines a key step in phytochrom-mediated regulation of HY-5.
phytochrome A signaling and COP1-mediated ubiquitylation are linked by the COP1- SPA1 interaction, which is light regulated.
